t: Babylon was a small town of the Akkadian Empire until Hammurabi, who ruled from 1792 to 1750 BCE, made it the capital of a kingdom that covered southern Mesopotamia.
It was destroyed by Sennacherib in 689 BCE and rebuilt, became the capital of the Neo-Babylonian Empire from 626 to 539 BCE, and then served as a capital of the Achaemenid Empire.
After the Hellenistic period it declined under Parthian, Sasanian and Muslim rule, and the last known habitation, a small village, dates from the 11th century CE.
dyk: Babylon has been estimated to have been the largest city in the world c. 1770 to c. 1670 BCE and again c. 612 to c. 320 BCE, and perhaps the first city to reach a population above 200,000.
ev: A year name of Shar-Kali-Sharri records the founding of temples in Babylon, its earliest reasonably firm mention
Hammurabi becomes king and builds Babylon into the capital of southern Mesopotamia
The city is thought to have been sacked by the Hittite king Mursili I
Sennacherib of Assyria destroys the city
Cyrus the Great takes Babylon and ends the Neo-Babylonian Empire
Alexander the Great enters Babylon after the Battle of Gaugamela
Robert Koldewey begins the first scientific excavations
UNESCO inscribes Babylon as a World Heritage Site

f.founded: First mentioned in the reign of the Akkadian king Shar-Kali-Sharri (2217 to 2193 BCE) as a town of the Akkadian Empire; classical writers gave foundation dates in the 23rd century BCE that cuneiform records do not confirm
f.where: On the lower Euphrates in southern Mesopotamia, near the modern city of Hillah in Iraq, about 85 kilometres south of Baghdad
f.known: The Code of Hammurabi; the Old and Neo-Babylonian empires; Esagila and the ziggurat Etemenanki; the Ishtar Gate; the Hanging Gardens, whose existence is disputed; the exile of the Jews in the Hebrew Bible; the Tower of Babel; Babylonian astronomy
f.today: The site is a ruin field near Hillah in Iraq, inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2019.
